==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{uder|en|frm|dividende|}}, from {{uder|en|la|dīvidendum||thing to be divided}}, future passive participle of {{m|la|dīvidō||to divide}}, {{surf|en|divide|-end|nocap=1}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈdɪvɪdɛnd/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-dividend.ogg|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|finance}} A [[cash]] [[payment]] of [[money]] by a [[company]] to its [[shareholder]]s, usually made [[periodically]] (e.g., [[quarterly]] or [[annually]]).
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1861|title=Laws of Pennsylvania of the Session of 1861|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=MhNAAAAAYAAJ&dq=%22twelve%20per%20centum%22&pg=PA511#v=onepage&q&f=false|page=511
|passage=On all '''dividends''' which do not exceed six per centum per annum, eight per centum; on '''dividends''' exceeding six per centum and not exceeding seven per centum, a tax of nine per centum...}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Paul R. La Monica|title=As markets wobble, buy the stocks that pay you back|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/09/14/investing/stocks-dividends-yield-income|date=2022-09-14|passage=Quarterly or annual '''dividend''' payments provide good income streams for investors who need cash in the short-term. And for those playing the longer game, '''dividends''' can be reinvested to buy even more shares in those same companies.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250724175551/https://edition.cnn.com/2022/09/14/investing/stocks-dividends-yield-income|archivedate=24 July 2025}}
# {{lb|en|arithmetic}} A number or [[expression]] that is to be divided by another.
#: {{ux|en|In "42 ÷ 3" the '''dividend''' is the 42.}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively}} {{U|beneficial}} [[result]]s from a [[metaphorical]] [[investment]] (of [[time]], [[effort]], etc.)
#: {{ux|en|His 10,000 hours of practice and recitals eventually paid '''dividends''' when he become first-chair violinist.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Slow Burn: Dead Fire, Book 4:|url=https://books.google.com/books?isbn=1499118910|author=Bobby Adair |year=2014|passage=The money I'd spent on getting scuba certified was about to pay a dividend. My half-baked escape plan came together.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Frida Ghitis|title=The GOP’s xenophobia is fueling toxic culture of hate|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/19/opinions/xenophobia-republicans-anti-asian-american-crimes-ghitis|date=2021-03-19|passage=The United States is not the only country where xenophobia pays '''dividends''' for politicians.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706000750/https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/19/opinions/xenophobia-republicans-anti-asian-american-crimes-ghitis/|archivedate=6 July 2022}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[pay out]] a dividend.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1997|title=Shareholder Rights, Oppression and Good Faith|page=40
|passage=He held instead that the words "sell or otherwise dispose of" in Clause 2 of the Shareholders' Agreement prevented the '''dividending''' of the shares in Hawker Holdings to the shareholders of Hawker Siddeley {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Kevin K. Boeh; Paul W. Beamish|title=Mergers and Acquisitions: Text and Cases|page=324
|passage=Therefore, $125 million of 1983 Preferred Shares (Blue Jay) would be tendered for retirement with $135 million of the $370 million '''dividended''' up to Blue Jay.}}
